# Recovery Assertion

## H1 — Goal

Create `util.mjs` exporting `stableSlug(s)` that lowercases ASCII letters, trims whitespace, replaces runs of non-alphanumeric characters with `-`, and removes leading/trailing `-`. The overall goal also requires `tests.mjs` using `node:assert` with at least three cases, including the empty string.

## H2 — Handoff Revision

The governed handoff is `handoff.md` at revision `8ef376afc183a4a3c190f225e068fe1295cdda013ab7ce933e383ea34312ec64`, based on commit `db38361a0d3ea322913a3deba9dfc46e16acb89c`.

## H3 — Verified State

No work is verified. The journal contains only initialization and preparation of round `R-01`, slice `S1`. It contains no Gate PASS, independent-review PASS, or Conductor-authored bound verification receipt.

## H4 — Unverified / In-Progress State

Slice `S1` is prepared but not verified. Its contracted outcome is that direct inspection accepts `util.mjs` as exporting the required `stableSlug` behavior. The slice target `util.mjs` was observed with no content. This is only a worktree observation: its commit status and provenance are unestablished, and it must not be treated as progress or completed work.

## H5 — Pending Action

The pending governed work is slice `S1`: implement the contracted `stableSlug` export in `util.mjs`, restricted to the stated lowercase, trim, non-alphanumeric run replacement, and leading/trailing dash removal behavior. After that bounded implementation, execution must stop for the governed Gate, independent review, and Conductor verification process.

## H6 — Blockers

No substantive blocker is recorded. No failed attempt, retry condition, replacement slice, replan reason, or verification failure appears in the ledger. The absence of deterministic checks in this slice does not authorize self-verification.

## H7 — Legal Next Action

The legal next execution action is the first bounded implementation attempt for slice `S1` in `util.mjs`, one of the contract’s allowed paths. It must remain within the current slice and stop on scope drift. This recovery assertion itself performs no implementation, file write, test execution, or completion declaration.

## H8 — Non-Goals and Forbidden Scope

No scope beyond the stated task is authorized. Work in `.tad/scripts/`, `.claude/`, and `.tad/hooks/` is forbidden. Starting another slice, implementing the overall testing requirement as self-authorized extra work, inspecting hidden acceptance, redoing verified work, and declaring the goal complete are outside the current authority. Strict Phase 2 also denies executor shell/Bash use and agent spawning.

## S1 — Why the Next Action Is Legal

Round `R-01` explicitly assigns slice `S1`, maps it to `SC-1`, names `util.mjs` as an allowed path, and defines the required implementation outcome. No prior attempt or verified result supersedes that contract, so a bounded first implementation of `util.mjs` is the uniquely supported next execution action.

## S2 — Why Verified Work Must Not Be Redone

The execution packet expressly forbids redoing verified work, and the quality policy allows zero repeated verified actions. Although nothing is verified yet, any later Conductor-bound verified result must be preserved rather than repeated; a candidate checkpoint, ordinary file state, or executor assertion cannot alter that boundary.

## S3 — Why Blind Retry or Self-Completion Is Unavailable

There is no recorded failed attempt to retry, no replacement slice, and no replan authorization. A blind retry therefore has no ledger basis. Self-completion is unavailable because verification can advance only through a bound receipt written by a Conductor distinct from the executor after both the existing Gate and an independent review pass. Executor prose, direct inspection alone, uncommitted observations, or a self-authored receipt cannot establish verification or completion.

## S4 — Rejected Actions and Claims

Rejected are treating the observed empty or otherwise uncommitted worktree
